headline_seed: Comey's seashell post got him indicted. But experts are sceptical the government can win
description_seed: Acting AG Todd Blanche said the case was investigated for months, adding "it's serious when you threaten the president."

what: Comey's seashell post got him indicted. But experts are sceptical the government can win

clean_source_blocks.text: Acting AG Todd Blanche said the case was investigated for months, adding "it's serious when you threaten the president."

"Prosecutors would need to prove that the seashell display was 'true threat,' which the Supreme Court has defined as a serious expression conveying that a speaker means to commit an act of unlawful violence," Barbara McQuade, a former US attorney for the Eastern District of Michigan who now teaches at the University of Michigan.

The justice department argues that a "reasonable recipient who is familiar with the circumstances would interpret as a serious expression of an intent to do harm to the President of the United States."
The government also must show that Comey was reckless in making his post, and knew the risks of doing so, McQuade said.
